---
title: 'Rehearse a release'
status: implemented
description: 'Build, sign and check a store release with Google Play and App Store Connect, without submitting anything.'
---

A rehearsal runs a release pipeline exactly as the release would: it builds,
signs, and then asks Google Play and App Store Connect whether they would take
the result. Nothing is submitted, released or sent to testers. Use it before a
release that matters, after changing signing, or when someone new runs their
first release.

## What you need

- Developer access or higher to the app.
- A pipeline that publishes to Google Play, the App Store, or both. A pipeline
  that publishes to no store has nothing to rehearse.
- A runner with the Oore version that has rehearsals. An older runner builds
  the rehearsal but uploads nothing and checks nothing.

## Rehearse

1. Open the app's **Releases** tab and choose **Rehearse a release**.
2. Pick the pipeline, the branch or commit and the workflow, as for a real
   release. Release notes you write here are checked too.
3. Choose **Rehearse**.

The build page says **Rehearsal · nothing submitted** beside its status, and
notifications add "(rehearsal, nothing submitted)" to the pipeline name.

From the CLI, add `--rehearsal` to
[`oore build run`](/reference/cli/oore-build-run).

## What it checks

For **Google Play**, the runner opens an edit, uploads the app bundle, sets
the track and the release notes, and asks Play to validate the edit. It then
deletes the edit without committing it, so nothing reaches any track. Play
reports a version code that is already used, a package name that does not
match, missing listing details, and a service account without access.

For the **App Store**, the runner checks the signed IPA, the app icon, the
release notes and the listing, then runs Apple's own validation
(`altool --validate-app`) with the pipeline's App Store Connect key. Apple
reports problems such as a build number that is already used, a missing
entitlement or an invalid icon.

Oore also adds the pipeline's store readiness checks, the same ones shown on
the pipeline's **Publishing** tab.

## Read the result

When the rehearsal finishes, the build page shows one of these:

- **Ready to release**: every store would take it. Choose **Release this
  commit** to run the real release with the same pipeline, workflow and
  commit.
- **Fix N things before you release**: each item says what the store refused,
  with a link to the page in Play Console or App Store Connect that fixes it.
  Fix them, then choose **Re-run** on the build to rehearse again.
- **The rehearsal did not finish**: the build or a store check failed before
  the stores answered. The build log shows why.

A rehearsal checks both stores before it fails, so one run lists every fix.

## Good to know

- A release freeze does not stop a rehearsal, because nothing is released.
- The rehearsal uses a version code like any other build. The release that
  follows gets a higher one.
- The findings are also at `GET /v1/builds/{build_id}/rehearsal`.
